name: hunger chess with rich forage
summary: At the start of each of your turns you collect 2 coins for every piece of yours on your back rank. You start with 10.
Every move costs coins: the further from your back rank a piece lands, the more it pays. A pawn pays 1 coin a rank, a knight, bishop, rook or queen 2 a rank, the king nothing.
A move you cannot pay for cannot be made. Instead of moving you may pass, unless you are in check.
Taking a piece earns you its booty from the bank: 1 coin for a pawn, 2 for any other piece.
A pawn that promotes pays for its own arrival and the new piece's: 21 coins for a queen.
description: Chess with supply lines and a rich farm. Every move is paid for out of a purse, and a piece costs more the further from home it lands. The coins come from home: every piece still on your back rank pays two a turn, so a full back rank earns sixteen, more than the dearest ordinary move, and the purse soon reaches its limit of 99. The trade the game keeps offering, develop a piece and lose its income or keep it home to fund an attack, is gentler when the farm is this rich: a player can afford to send pieces out early and still pay for them. It is kept to show how tight the economy should be, set beside the same game at one coin a piece.

provenance.note: A variation of Hunger Chess, a playtested variant sent in to this project by its designer.
